text:
maya: heads up — after the eu-west rolling drain this morning we've got a bunch of tiny leftover GPU nodes with single-slot pods. cluster looks highly fragmented and evictions are spiking.

sachin: saw that, most of the stranded nodes are in eu-west1-b. affinity + podTopologySpread prevented packing.

liam: any alerts? saw some 5xxs from model-serving during reschedules.

ops-bot: [alert] pod_eviction_count @ eu-west1-b increased from 3 -> 47 in the last 10m :rotating_light:

maya: yeah, two problems: (1) rolling drain set node taints for maintenance, drained too aggressively and left many single-gpu VMs, (2) our anti-affinity rules + requiredDuringScheduling prevented colocating small jobs.

dina: quick data point: `kubectl get nodes -o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,GPU:.metadata.labels.gpu,ALLOC:.status.allocatable.gpu` shows ~18 nodes with 1 allocatable gpu and 0 pods except system.

harry: the descheduler job didn't kick in because it checks only for long-term imbalance (24h). this is a fast transient.

sachin: proposal: temporarily relax anti-affinity for batch/pod type `low-priority` with a PodDisruptionBudget override so we can binpack until capacity stabilizes.

liam: +1 but we need a safe guard — only allow packing on nodes with label `gpu-pack-allow=true` and avoid instances in AZ eu-west1-a to keep cross-az traffic low.

maya: for immediate mitigation I'm going to: 1) patch descheduler to run a one-off `RemoveDuplicates` pass with a 10m window, 2) create K8s job to set `gpu-pack-allow=true` on 12 nodes, 3) roll out a k8s mutating webhook that rewrites strict anti-affinity for pods with label `workload=best-effort` (manual override).

dina: can you post the exact kubectl patches? ops needs to coordinate with infra before node labels change.

maya: sure — `kubectl label node <node> gpu-pack-allow=true --overwrite` and descheduler run: `kubectl apply -f descheduler-oneoff.yaml && kubectl create job descheduler-quick --from=cronjob/descheduler` (will attach the yaml).

harry: also watch egress/cross-az billing — last time we spilled across AZs it added ~$2k/day. keep draining to same AZ where possible.

sachin: long term: we should add a transient-aware packing policy in the scheduler that considers recent drains and allows temporary relaxation of node anti-affinity for compatible workloads. also increase descheduler frequency to 1h during rolling updates.

liam: logging: can we add an annotation on evicted pods `eviction.reason=fragmentation` so it's easier to query in the console?

maya: done — added a patch to eviction controller to annotate. will monitor for 30m and revert labels if latencies spike.

ops-bot: [note] Incident channel created: #inc-eu-west-gpu-packing — linking back to this thread.

dina: any objections from security or cost teams? cc @finance for cost FYI.

sachin: pinging finance and sec in #vendors — but immediate fix is infra-side, low risk.

liam: ok let's proceed. I'll run smoke tests on model-serving once packing settles. pls post results here. :thumbsup:

maya: will do. updating runbook and adding a short checklist so oncall can repeat safely.

harry: tl;dr: drain => tiny leftover nodes + strict anti-affinity => fragmentation => evictions + cross-AZ reschedules. mitigation: label nodes, one-off descheduler, relax rules for best-effort, monitor cost/latency.

maya: closing loop: initial pack op completed, eviction rate down to 6 in last 5m. will leave labels for 2h and then revert. thanks all. :pray:
